**Casey Delgado**
[Street Address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

Date: [Date of this letter]

CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield
Member Services Department
[Address printed on my member ID card]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 25, 2026**
- **Member:** Casey Delgado
- **Member ID:** W200134956
- **Reference number:** POC-6B51D0A6AA-87439
- **Service denied:** ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
- **Ordering surgeon:** Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** EviCore by Evernorth Clinical Guidelines CMM-312: Knee Surgery–Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2025 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-312%20Knee%20Surg%20Arthro_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.25.2025.pdf

Dear Member Services Department,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), which CareFirst issued on August 25, 2026 under reference number POC-6B51D0A6AA-87439. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking CareFirst to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records that were submitted address the criteria in the plan's own guideline point by point. Below I set out the plan's language alongside what my chart says.

---

### 1. The plan's imaging criterion

The guideline states:

> "MRI, CT arthrogram, or arthroscopy shows a tear/disruption or significant laxity of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)"

My MRI of the knee dated July 5, 2026 shows a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern. The menisci are intact and there is no significant arthritis. This is the imaging study the criterion calls for, and it shows the finding the criterion describes.

### 2. The plan's physical examination criterion

The guideline states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates ANY of the following findings:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of findings. One of the listed findings I have been given is:

> "Positive anterior drawer test"

My examination is documented as showing positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. I do not want to characterize my chart as saying anything more specific than it says. If CareFirst requires a particular named test from that list, I ask that the reviewer identify which finding on the list was considered missing, so that Dr. Reyes can point to the corresponding entry in the exam note or document it directly.

### 3. The plan's function and instability criteria

The guideline states:

> "Function-limiting knee pain and/or loss of knee function which interferes with ANY of the following:"

Among the items on that list that I have been given are:

> "Abil ity to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living"

> "N eed to return to activities that require cutting, pivoting, and/or agility in which ACL insufficiency may predispose to further instability episodes that may result in new articular or meniscal cartilage injuries"

My records document 14 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest, recurrent instability with pivoting, and two episodes of the knee giving way on stairs.

The guideline also states:

> "Individual reports knee inst ability which is noted as giving way, subjective weakness, or buckling"

My chart records exactly that: recurrent instability with pivoting, and the knee giving way twice on stairs.

### 4. The plan's conservative-care criterion

The guideline states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration"

My records document the following provider-directed non-surgical care:

- **Supervised physical therapy** for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, from April 1, 2026 to July 8, 2026 — 14 weeks, 24 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- **NSAIDs** for 8 months, with inadequate relief;
- **Corticosteroid injection** on May 9, 2026, which gave approximately 3 weeks of partial relief.

My supervised, provider-directed physical therapy ran for 14 weeks, from April 1, 2026 through July 8, 2026, with 24 visits completed, and it is documented in a discharge note that was part of the packet. The medication trial and the injection are documented as well, and neither resolved my symptoms.

Because that criterion is met on its face, I do not believe the plan's exception pathway needs to be reached. For completeness, the guideline also states:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required if there is an acute injury setting and joint instability has been documented with ANY of the following additional conditions:"

and lists, among those conditions:

> "A confirmed ACL tear and a repairable meniscus tear"

> "Concomitant ligament injuries (i.e., multi-ligamentous knee injury) that require reconstruction to provide stability)"

I am relying on the completed course of provider-directed non-surgical management described above, not on this exception.

---

### A note on what I have been able to quote

The excerpts above are the only portions of CMM-312 I have in front of me. Several of them end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced for me, so there may be criteria in the policy that I have not seen and therefore have not addressed. I am not quoting or characterizing any part of the guideline beyond the text set out above.

### My request

The denial says the documentation was incomplete. The records summarized above — the July 5, 2026 MRI report, the physical therapy discharge note covering April 1 through July 8, 2026, the medication and injection history, and Dr. Reyes's clinical notes describing my instability and exam findings — were part of the prior authorization packet and speak directly to the guideline's criteria. I respectfully ask CareFirst to:

1. **Overturn the denial** and authorize ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888); or, if that is not the outcome,
2. **Identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria in CMM-312 that the reviewer found unsupported**, and the specific document or finding that was considered missing, so that Dr. Reyes and I can supply it promptly; and
3. **Confirm that the reviewer had the complete packet**, including the MRI report and the physical therapy discharge note.

I am happy to have Dr. Reyes's office resend any record at no delay, and I am available for a peer-to-peer discussion between Dr. Reyes and your reviewing physician. Please also confirm whether a physician with orthopedic expertise reviewed this request.

Per the denial notice, my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of notification — **by February 21, 2027** — and I am submitting it to the Member Services Department at the address printed on my member ID card, as the notice and CareFirst's appeal instructions direct. The Member Services telephone number on my ID card is also available if your office needs to reach me about this appeal.

Thank you for taking another look at this. I would like to get back to walking stairs and daily activities without my knee giving way, and I am asking that the decision be reconsidered against the plan's own stated criteria.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Casey Delgado**
Member ID: W200134956
Date: [Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated August 25, 2026 (Ref. POC-6B51D0A6AA-87439)
- MRI report, knee, dated July 5, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (April 1, 2026 – July 8, 2026, 24 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery — [dates of visits]
- Medication and injection records, including corticosteroid injection dated May 9, 2026

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
